sermon.title: Prophets and Teachers
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer explains the office of a prophet: a prediction, a sign, a message that lines up with the Bible—the real proof—and fulfillment. He warns about false prophets, recalls what he saw in decades of awakening, and shows prophets and teachers at work in Acts, urging believers to continue in the apostles’ doctrine and the more excellent way of love.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: This recording’s captions were especially rough; many caption fixes were needed and nine phrases were not clear. Points to check: Hezekiah’s sundial moved “20 degrees, forty minutes” (Isaiah 38:8 says ten degrees); “98 percent” of healing prayers unanswered; President Carter attending a segregated church; Adam the first prophet. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Catholic church “a joke” in the Dark Ages, Republican debate and politicians, the Beatles and Hollywood, healing-line fakery, a woman in Alabama with a familiar spirit.

chunks.section_question: Why aren’t all believers prophets or teachers?
chunks.short_answer: 1 Corinthians 12:28 ranks apostles, then the office of the prophet, then teachers—but are all prophets or teachers? No; a body that was all eyes or all tongue couldn’t function. If God makes you the little toe, you are as great in his eyes as any apostle. Jesus promised to send prophets and scribes (Matthew 23:34, Luke 11:49).

chunks.short_answer: 2 Thessalonians 2:3: the day will not come except there be a falling away first. He says it already happened in the Dark Ages, when truth and repentance were lost. Acts 3:20–21: heaven retains Christ until the restoration of all things—like restoring an old car to original condition.

chunks.section_question: Can the elect be deceived by signs and wonders?
